title: A machine for a polynomial-time function
statement: Let $f$ be a polynomial-time computable function from binary words to binary words. There exist a finite Boolean Turing machine $W$, states $\mathrm{entry}$ and $\mathrm{exit}$ of $W$, and natural numbers $a,d$ with at least one work tape, such that for every physical input word $x$ and argument word $\mathrm{arg}$, there is a time $t$ with $0<t\le a(|\mathrm{arg}|+1)^d$. At every integer time $j$ with $0<j<t$, the machine started on $x$ in state $\mathrm{entry}$ with $\mathrm{arg}$ on tape zero and all other work tapes empty is not in state $\mathrm{exit}$; at time $t$ its configuration is exactly the one with state $\mathrm{exit}$, $f(\mathrm{arg})$ on tape zero, all other work tapes empty, and the input head, work-tape heads, and output tape in their standard initial positions and contents.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is any physical Boolean input word
the machine has at least one work tape
no intermediate time $j$ with $0<j<t$ has state $\mathrm{exit}$
the time-$t$ configuration equals the specified exit configuration
replaced: For every polynomial-time computable string function $f$, there are a machine with at least one work tape, entry and exit controls, and constants $a, d$ such that for every physical input and argument word, the machine started at the entry over the argument's state word reaches, at a strictly positive first exit within $a(|arg|+1)^d$ steps, exactly the state word of $f$ of the argument, with all scratch cells and heads restored after each request.
